text: Is the date on the bag the roast date or when it goes bad? I could not tell and I almost threw it out.
I went on holiday and got three bags I could not drink. I love the coffee, but I came home to a pile.
I am embarrassed to order decaf, it feels like admitting defeat. I wish the label was a bit prouder about it.
My pour over tastes sour and I follow the recipe exactly. I have tried three kettles and nothing changes.
I threw out a bag because the date looked like an expiry. Only later did a friend say it was a roast date.
We need the beans on Tuesday morning, not Wednesday afternoon. Our baristas run short and the weekend rush has no mercy.
There is no way to skip a delivery without emailing you. It should be one click, honestly.
How many grams of coffee per cup, is there a simple rule? Every site says something different.
People at the office judge me for decaf. I have started hiding the bag in my desk drawer.
Please put roasted on in bold next to the date. I bought two bags and still was not sure which was fresher.
The playlist in the shop is fantastic, who picks it? I would happily pay for the Sunday mix.
Let me pause for a week without cancelling. I do not want to lose my place, I just need a breather.
The grinder I bought makes either dust or boulders. I do not know if it is me or the machine.
Our baristas run out on Mondays so a set delivery day matters. Can you promise the same day every week?
My customers keep asking if the best by date means it is stale. I work in a bakery and I am never sure what to tell them.
Is your decaf actually good or just an afterthought? I have been burnt by weak decaf before.
Could you stock oat milk in the cafe? Half my group will not come in without it.
Founder note: three questions this week about sour coffee, all grind related. Worth a short guide.
I would love bags in a gift box for my dad's birthday. Is there a packaging option that is not plastic?
